title: My First Week at Instituto Dourados: Analyzing COVID Data from the Reserva Indígena de Dourados
text:
What Makes This Data Special
What struck me most about this dataset is what it records. Instead of just biological characteristics like height or age, the researchers recorded social information: which aldeia the person lived in, their Indigenous ethnicity, which COVID variant infected them, and the date of detection.
This reflects a core idea at Instituto Dourados: epidemiology includes social science. Understanding who interacts with whom helps us understand how disease spreads and how to design better public health interventions.

title: My First Week at Instituto Dourados: Analyzing COVID Data from the Reserva Indígena de Dourados
text:
What I Did in R
Using R, I ran code to visualize how many COVID infections were recorded over time in the Reserva. Now I can use the same code to create the same style visualizations for new data, real or simulated.

title: My First Week at Instituto Dourados: Analyzing COVID Data from the Reserva Indígena de Dourados
text:
Reflection
This was my first experience analyzing real epidemiological data using R. It was challenging but rewarding to work with data that has real implications for public health in Brazil.

title: About
text:
My Research
I am currently a Junior Research Intern at Instituto Dourados, where I work on social epidemiology research focused on Indigenous public health in the Reserva Indígena de Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil.

title: Mariana Barreto Alcantara
text:
I am Mariana Barreto Alcantara, a first-year student at the University of California, Berkeley, double majoring in Neuroscience and Business Administration. Originally from Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, I have spent the past four years in the United States and am passionate about applying the knowledge and skills I have gained here to strengthen Brazilian public health.
As a Junior Research Intern, I contribute to public health communications aimed at educating communities on healthy living practices and the role of scientific research in promoting well-being. My work also spans social sciences and computational epidemiology, where I help develop systems to visualize public health data and identify the social factors that most significantly influence disease spread across different contexts.
Driven by my roots and my interdisciplinary background, I am committed to bridging scientific research and community impact in Brazil.
